overall_summary: Space anomalies and extreme exoplanets are driving the channel's highest engagement and views, with videos like 'The Planet of Burning Ice' and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' consistently crossing 1,000 views. Conversely, psychology, brain facts, and basic animal trivia are severely underperforming, rarely exceeding 100 views.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,014 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) represent the channel's top tier of performance.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme exoplanet environments, using high-contrast visual hooks and sensory descriptions (e.g., raining glass, burning ice, ruby storms) in the first 3 seconds.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees' (302 views) and 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (263 views) performed well above the channel's average baseline.
winning_patterns.action: Create content around counter-intuitive timeline comparisons, historical overlaps, and physics-based age paradoxes.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 53 views across multiple uploads) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) failed to gain any traction.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic psychological advice or brain hacks, as they lack the visual and curiosity-driven appeal of cosmic content.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118 views) and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views) underperformed.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid basic, textbook animal facts; if covering animals, shift to cinematic survival narratives or deep-sea mysteries.

next_video.concept: The planet where it snows actual metal and rains acid.

next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that this isn't a sci-fi world light-years away, but Venus, right in our own solar system, where mountain peaks are capped with metallic frost made of galena and bismuth.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful exoplanet/cosmic weather trend while introducing a shocking twist about our own solar system, keeping the duration under 20 seconds for optimal completion rate.

experiment: Test a 3-part series on 'Cosmic Horrors' focusing on terrifying space phenomena (like rogue black holes or zombie stars) to bridge the gap between space facts and horror/mystery micro-stories.
